course_name_original: Lithium-Ion Batteries: Characterization, Modelling and Applications in Industry
course_name_en: Lithium-Ion Batteries: Characterization, Modelling and Applications in Industry
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematics, general physics, and electrical circuits at undergraduate engineering level.
Students should be able to perform simple engineering calculations, use units correctly, rearrange formulas, and interpret basic graphs.
Basic high-school chemistry (moles, concentration, redox reactions, oxidation states) is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: The chemical, electrochemical, electrical, and thermal principles governing the operation of lithium-ion batteries, including the relationships between cell structure, materials, and performance parameters
The main quantities and concepts used to describe lithium-ion batteries, including capacity, energy, power, C-rate, SoC, SoH, DoD, efficiency, and ageing mechanisms
The main lithium-ion chemistries, production processes, characterization methods, testing procedures, and safety requirements used in industrial practice
the basic approaches to lithium-ion battery modelling, including electrical, thermal, and simplified electrochemical models, and their role in battery analysis and system design
the principles of using lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles, battery energy storage systems, and other industrial applications, including technical, operational, and environmental aspects
perform basic calculations related to battery chemistry and electrochemistry, including stoichiometry, concentrations, electrochemical potential, capacity, energy, power, and efficiency
analyse the influence of load, temperature, and operating conditions on the performance, efficiency, and degradation of lithium-ion batteries
interpret the results of basic battery measurements and tests and assess the condition and operating properties of a lithium-ion cell on the basis of measurement data
select a simplified battery model for a given engineering problem and use it to describe, analyse, and predict the basic behaviour of a cell or battery system
evaluate the suitability of lithium-ion batteries for selected industrial applications, taking into account safety, operating requirements, economic factors, and environmental impact
critically assess technical data, datasheets, and test results related to lithium-ion batteries and continuously update knowledge in response to the rapid development of battery technologies
take into account engineering responsibility when assessing the safety, durability, and environmental impact of lithium-ion batteries and battery systems
act in a professional and responsible manner when solving engineering problems related to the design, testing, and operation of battery systems

syllabus_topics: From atoms to batteries: chemical foundations needed to understand how lithium-ion cells store and release energy.
Electrochemical potential, redox reactions, and the Nernst equation as the basis for battery voltage and driving forces.
Inside a lithium-ion cell: structure, materials, and key performance descriptors such as capacity, energy, power, SoC, SoH, DoD, and C-rate.
Lithium-ion chemistries in practice: anodes, cathodes, electrolytes, separators, and the trade-offs behind different cell designs.
Ageing and degradation: SEI formation, equivalent cycles, loss of performance, and the factors limiting battery lifetime.
How batteries are made: industrial production, assembly steps, and the role of manufacturing quality in performance and safety.
Electrical behaviour of batteries: resistance, conductivity, ohmic losses, load effects, and transient response represented by RC-based models.
Charge-transfer kinetics, efficiency, and thermal behaviour: how electrochemical and thermal processes shape real battery operation.
Battery characterization and testing: measurements, test procedures, standards, and interpretation of battery performance data.
Battery modelling fundamentals: electrical, thermal, and simplified electrochemical models for analysis, prediction, and engineering applications.
From cell to system: lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles, BESS, and other industrial applications, including safety and environmental aspects.
Hands-on tutorial sessions and project focused on solving real battery engineering problems through calculations, test-data interpretation, and introductory battery modelling with PyBaMM.

assessment_methods.method: Report on completion of a practical placement

assessment_rules: The final grade is an average of the exam and project assignment. Students who are absent need to complete the associated exercises on their own. All project meetings are obligatory.
